title: Coupling live-cell imaging and in situ isolation of the same single cell to profile the transient states of predicted drug-tolerant cells
protocol: Add 1 mL of rat tail collagen coating solution (40 μg/mL) on the FrameSlide membrane.
Aspirate back 400 μL and let incubate with 600 μL on the FrameSlide.
Incubate for 2 h at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Quick wash membrane twice (30 s) with 600 μL fresh 1× PBS.
Count cells from a 100 mm dish.
Resuspend cells to reach a density of 6000 cells in 700 μL of imaging medium.
Add 700 μL of cell suspension to the coated FrameSlides PET.
Incubate for 30 min under the tissue culture hood to allow homogeneous cell seeding.
Place the FrameSlides PET on the SlideHolder and incubate overnight at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Do not add more than 800 μL of medium to the FrameSlide.
Place the FrameSlide on a clean bench for 30 minutes before moving it to the incubator if needed for homogeneous cell seeding.
Perform live-cell treatment as required.
Conduct video microscopy.
Turn on microscope and workstation.
Turn on the Temperature Controller using the power switch on the back of the unit.
Press the Temp button on the front of the controller to display the current temperature set point.
Use the Up and Down buttons to change the temperature to 37°C.
Press Display to save changes.
Press the Config button until “Fan Air Flow Set Point” reaches 30%.
Press Display to save changes.
Check the temperature inside the environmental chamber.
Modify the temperature setpoint if necessary.
Allow ample time (minimum 6 h) for the system to reach a stable temperature/CO2 environment.
Verify that the humidifier is between ½ and ¾ full of deionized water.
Turn on the premixed gas and set regulator between 5–10 PSI.
Switch the flowmeter to the “ON” position.
Slowly turn the knob to adjust flow rate between 40–50 (160–207 mL/min).
Mount the FrameSlides PET on the stage with the Zeiss logo on the left.
Insert the SlideHolder with the red pine on the left.
Place a cell cover over the samples.
Verify that the gasket on the cover surrounds the outer edge of the SlideHolder.
Check the imaging medium on the slide to ensure it does not dry up at 37°C.
Click on the Start SoftWoRx™ icon.
From the main menu, choose File and Acquire (Resolve3D) to initialize the system.
Rotate objective turret until 20× objective is in the active position.
Update selection in the Lens drop down menu.
Use the Polychroic drop down menu and select Quad.
Set the Binning drop down menu to 2 × 2.
Focus on the sample and find a region of interest.
Check Filter Monitor windows to ensure Ex and Em filters match for every channel (CFP, YFP, and POL).
Open the YFP channel and click on the Continuous Acquisition button to focus on regions with up to 20 well-separated cells.
Stop Continuous Acquisition.
Select the Experiment button in the Resolve3D window.
Uncheck the Use fast acquisition button.
Uncheck the checkboxes “Use fast acquisition” and “Z Sectioning” in the sectioning panel.
Ensure that the exposure in the channels is set between 25 and 80 ms depending on the fluorescence intensity.
Select 32% transmittance for both fluorescence channels.
Select 5% transmittance for the POL channel.
Set the time-lapse parameters.
Activate the option “Maintain Focus with UltimateFocus” option.
Uncheck the Z-sectioning button in the sectioning tab.
Activate appropriate channels (CFP, YFP, and POL) in the Channels tab.
Set transmittance to 32% and exposure time to 80 ms for both CFP and YFP channels.
Set transmittance to 10% and exposure time to 5 ms for the polarized channel.
Determine exposure and transmittance parameters to achieve a signal-to-noise ratio greater than 1.5 for both CFP and YFP.
Activate the Time-lapse tab.
Set the time between points in the time-lapse to 3 minutes.
Set the total time of the time-lapse up to 50 minutes.
Select a maximum of three non-overlapping fields with more than three cells each using the joystick.
Place selected fields towards the center of the wells.
Click “Mark Point”.
Save the point list.
Replace a point by clicking on “Replace Point”.
Visit each point using the camera and refine the focus position (z axis) using the dZ button in the resolve 3D window.
Click the Replace Point button to save the update position.
Activate the Point tab and list all points you want to visit.
Save the experiment.
Click the Run button and start acquiring for up to 30 min.
Stop the acquisition and proceed to the experiment.
Prepare 800 μL of imaging medium containing 25 ng/mL rhTRAIL.
Open the environmental chamber.
Aspirate 700 μL of the imaging media.
Add 800 μL of imaging media containing rhTRAIL (within 5 seconds).
Click the Run button and start acquiring for up to 50 min.
Cool cells by gently plunging the FrameSlide PET into a 50 mL tube filled with PBS containing Ca2+/Mg2+, placed on ice.
Import DvtoZeiss.
Execute DvtoZeiss.allConversion with Zeiss_init, DV_init, path_to_dv_pts_file, name_dv_pts_file, path_saved_zeiss_file, and name_saved_zeiss_file for obtaining coefficients of linear regression.
Execute DvtoZeiss.allConversion with path_to_dv_pts_file, name_dv_pts_file, path_saved_zeiss_file, and name_saved_zeiss_file for point list conversion using marker points.
Execute DvtoZeiss.allConversion with A, B, path_to_dv_pts_file, name_dv_pts_file, path_saved_zeiss_file, and name_saved_zeiss_file for point list conversion using pre-obtained coefficients.
Open the raw image stack sequences in ImageJ software.
Select “Image”, then “Stacks”, followed by “Tools” and finally “Make Substack” from the main menu.
Specify the range and increment corresponding to each channel to create three different substacks: one for CFP, YFP, and polarized channels respectively.
Repeat step 23 for each channel.
Select the CFP substack.
Draw a single ROI in a background region.
Measure the pixel mean intensity using Analyze Menu then Measure or ctrl+m for stack 1 (CFP).
Select a region of interest in a background area.
Measure the average intensity of the pixels in the CFP channel.
Copy the same zone of interest to the YFP channel.
Measure the average intensity of the pixels in the YFP channel's background.
Open the Ratio Image plugin and enter settings for the background.
Create the ratiometric image by subtracting background intensities.
Copy the ROI to the YFP substack using Edit/Selection/Restore selection or ctrl+shift+E.
Measure the pixel mean intensity for substack 2 (YFP).
Open the Ratio Plus plugin.
Select the CFP substack in stack 1 and the YFP substack in stack 2.
Enter the background intensity value for the CFP channel.
Enter 50% of the intensity value for the YFP channel obtained from previous steps.
Generate a ratiometric stack in 32-bits format showing the CFP/YFP ratio.
In the Analyze menu, select Tools and ROI manager.
Draw one ROI for each cell in the ratiometric stack.
Select all the ROI.
Check the “Show All” and “Labels boxes”.
Click on “More” option and then “Multimeasures”.
Click on “measure all slices” and “one row per slice”.
Save the values of ratio intensities in a .csv spreadsheet for further analysis.
Read files for the experiment.
Process trajectories in the experiment.
Compute mean time derivative for FRET data.
Sort cells based on their computed derivatives.
Plot FRET trajectories of selected top and bottom responder cells.
Select top 7 high responder cells and bottom 7 low responder cells from tracked micro-dissection steps.
Turn on the laser for Zeiss PALM setup.
Turn on the microscope for Zeiss PALM setup.
Turn on the control box for Zeiss PALM setup.
Turn on the computer for Zeiss PALM setup.
Start MTB2004Configuration in Zeiss PALM setup.
Click Write configuration after settings are selected.
Start PALMRobo v4.2 in Zeiss PALM setup.
Start LPM and write configuration in Zeiss PALM setup.
Start Robot Controller – Open PALM Robo Software for Zeiss PALM setup.
Click on view default Bar config in the software.
Apply a collar correction to adjust the working distance for a FrameSlide: check on objective lens 20×, between 0 and dot (0.17 mm).
Define “collector type” for Zeiss PALM setup.
Click on “Autoconfig” button on the camera display panel for Zeiss PALM setup.
Click on “Autoconfiguration” in the “Camera” area.
Display laser intensity parameters for microdissection.
Arrange PCR tube caps as shown to avoid contact with cells or support membrane.
Lower caps into position for efficient cell catapulting.
Check the laser capture setup and check RoboMover.
Note initial resting value of Fine Adjust Z-Axis.
Adjust Z value to determine laser capture position: cap must come close to FrameSlide’s membrane without touching it.
Note adjusted Z value and return to its initial resting value.
Set up Köhler illumination as shown in the Zeiss tutorial video (exclude link).
Choose a fluorescent channel, for example FITC, to visualize cells of interest.
Select Microbeam Laser.
Set cut energy to 49.
Set LPC energy to 28.
Set cut focus to 75.
Set LPC focus to -1.
Reduce cutting speed to test the parameters of the laser.
Check PBS every 10 min for evaporation.
Draw a list of minimum 14 cells (7 high responders and 7 complete non-responders).
Take the Zeiss point list set as “Dot” and save as text file to import in the Palm List.
Turn the FrameSlide 90 degrees clockwise.
Add 800 μL fresh cold PBS.
Locate cells of interest and hit “Freeze.”
Circle the cell to add to the list, rename cell.
Go to the next field (region of interest containing the selected cells).
Pipette 4.3 μl of cell lysis buffer in each tube from a PCR strip tubes.
Remove medium with p1000 Pipet.
Place the cap, lower the cap (cap handler set Z-Axis to the cutting position noted in step 44).
Adjust the focus using the phase-contrast.
Ensure the cap strip is in position as shown.
Lower the cap strip to the slide.
Turn on FITC (or another available fluorescent channel) to visualize cells during the cut.
Hit laser cut.
Place cap in higher position using cap handler.
Move cap strip to next cell location.
Capture cells into PCR tube caps containing 4.3 μL capture lysis buffer.
When 8 cells are captured, place the caps on empty labeled tubes.
Spin the tubes immediately after capturing the cells.
Place tubes directly onto dry ice for rapid freezing.
Store the cell lysates in a freezer at -80°C for up to 1 month.
Laser capture single cells with predicted cell response.
Collect the captured single cells.
Lysate the collected cells in domed caps of 0.2 mL PCR tubes.
Store the lysates frozen until further processing.
Transfer the lysates to PCR tubes containing an RT mix and ERCC spike-ins.
Reverse transcribe the RNA using a primer that includes a priming site for amplification, a random sequence (UMI), a cell barcode (BC), and an Illumina Index Read (IIR).
Add a template switching oligonucleotide (TSO) to provide a second PCR priming site during RT.
Amplify the cDNA through PCR.
Tagment the 3′ biotinylated full-length cDNA with EZ-Tn5 transposase, which end-joins it with mosaic end adaptors.
Isolate the 3′ terminal fragments on Streptavidin beads.
Introduce sequences required for Illumina sequencing (P5, P7) by PCR before sequencing.
Prepare 0.2 mL PCR tubes with the pre-mix.
Thaw reagents on ice.
Add 2.43 μL of pre-mix containing ERCC-spike-In Mix, dNTPs, and reverse transcription primer to each tube.
Briefly centrifuge tubes after adding cells by microdissection.
Store single-cell in pre-mix at −80°C or transport in dry ice until further use.
Add 8.27 μL of reverse transcription buffer to each tube.
Add 4.53 mM DTT, 1.8 M Betaïne, and 10.8 mM MgCl2 to the tubes.
Add 3.62 μM template switching oligonucleotide and 0.6 U/μL RNAse IN Plus.
Add 7.5 U/μL Invitrogen SuperScript II reverse transcriptase to each tube.
Reverse transcribe each tube at 10 min at 25°C, followed by 90 min at 42°C, then 15 min at 70°C, and keep at 10°C until PCR amplification.
Amplify samples with KAPA HiFi Hotstart ready Mix for 20 cycles using forward PCR primer and biotinylated reverse PCR primer.
Incubate samples at 98°C for 3 min followed by 20 cycles of 98°C for 20 s, 64°C for 15 s, and 72°C for 6 min, then a final extension at 72°C for 5 min.
Pool the PCR amplified samples.
Purify pooled samples with 0.8× Beckman Coulter SPRIselect beads to remove primers and small DNA fragments.
Place on the magnet until the solution clears.
Remove the supernatant and wash with 200 μL of 85% EtOH.
Quick spin for 5 seconds.
Put back on the magnet and remove any remaining EtOH by pipetting.
Dry for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Take off the magnet.
Elute in 30 μL nuclease-free water by pipetting up and down 15 times.
Leave for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Put the tube back on the magnet.
Aspirate the supernatant when the solution clears.
Save the supernatant (cDNA) for the next step at room temperature if used immediately.
If not, store the supernatant at 4°C for up to 72 hours or at -20°C for up to 4 weeks.
Do not dry the pellet more than 2 minutes to avoid over-drying.
Purify a second time with SPRIselect beads (0.8×) if concentrating final amount of cDNA pools.
Elute in 12 μL nuclease-free water after purification.
Perform quality and quantity control with a BioAnalyzer High Sensitivity DNA kit on 1 μL of purified pooled cDNA.
Distribute the cDNAs between 200 bp to 9000 bp.
At room temperature, pipette 9 μL of cDNA and add 4 μL TAPS buffer (50 mM TAPS-NaOH, pH8.5, 25 mM MgCl2), 2 μL dimethylformamide, and 5 μL of transposon.
Incubate at 55°C for 7 minutes.
Cool the samples to 10°C for 5 minutes.
Add 4 μL of 0.1% SDS and incubate at 65°C for 10 minutes.
Cool samples to 4°C.
Pipette 24 μL Dynabeads® MyOne™ Streptavidin C1 beads into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Resuspend beads in 10.5 μL nuclease-free water.
Amplify 5′ terminal fragments in 25 μL with KAPA HiFi HotStart Ready Mix and primers.
Incubate at 75°C for 3 min followed by 98°C for 30 s, then proceed with 15 cycles of 98°C for 10 s, 55°C for 30 s, and 72°C for 30 s, ending with an extension step at 72°C for 2 min.
Fill the volume of Illumina library obtained to 100 μL.
Add 90 μL SPRIselect beads for size selection of fragments > 200 bp.
Mix 15 times and incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Place on the magnet, remove supernatant, wash with 85% EtOH, then dry 2 min at RT.
Elute library by pipetting 15 times with 10 μL nuclease-free water.
Incubate off the magnet for 2 min, place back on the magnet until solution clears, and pipette out supernatant.
Perform a quality and quantity control with a BioAnalyzer High Sensitivity DNA kit on 1 μL of purified libraries.
Distribute the final library between 200 bp to 550 bp, with a peak around 350 bp.
Sequence libraries using a NextSeq500/550 High Output V2 kit (75 cycles).
Allow up to 91 cycles with an index1 read of 20 nucleotides (8 bp cell barcode and 12 bp UMI).
Use custom sequencing primers for a read1 of 71 nucleotides for cDNA sequencing.
Produce Fastq files using Illumina bcl2fastq software.
Align the read1 against human build reference using a splice-aware aligner, such as STAR.
Obtain a BAM file composed of SAM records describing how/where cDNA reads aligned to the reference genome.
